instructions.content: Fetch the repo README and linked docs, and record tool name, author or org, license, language, latest version or commit, and primary URL.
Derive the slug as <author-or-org>-<tool-name>, with no exceptions.
Search REVIEWED.md and references/REFERENCE_INDEX.md for the slug or repo URL; if already present, report it and stop.
Classify the tool with one or more tags from the controlled list in references/classification-guide.md.
Assess scope fit (in scope, borderline, out of scope) before writing the summary, and note any borderline ruling in REVIEWED.md rather than silently including or excluding it.
Read assets/templates/REFERENCE-tool.yaml and create references/<slug>.md with all required frontmatter fields followed by the required sections.
Populate TL;DR (3 to 8 bullets), What's novel, Architecture overview (N/A where not applicable), Deployment model, Self-reported metrics (as reported) and Open questions.
Keep language precise, do not pad, and mark all unverified claims.
Ask whether to vendor the repo as a git submodule in tools/<repo-name>/; when vendored, set local_clone to the submodule path relative to the document.
Add a REVIEWED.md summary row (reverse-chronological, type tool, disposition pending).
Add a REFERENCE_INDEX.md row under the most relevant category.
Report what was created, then ask whether to promote, vendor, keep as pending, or skip with reasoning.
When promotion is confirmed, create analysis/ANALYSIS-<slug>.md from assets/templates/ANALYSIS-tool.yaml and change the REVIEWED.md disposition from pending to analysis.

After the analysis, create benchmarks/sources/<slug>-repro.md from the REPRO template; look for the harness in benchmarks/, eval/, evals/, then scripts/; set harness_present, harness_path and an allowed outcome value.
Validate completed files with scripts/validate-reference-tool.sh and scripts/validate-analysis-tool.sh.
NEVER omit YAML frontmatter; open every file with a --- block containing all required fields.
NEVER treat self-reported benchmarks as verified; mark them (as reported).
NEVER skip the duplicate check before creating files.
NEVER vendor without user confirmation (no git submodule add during triage).
NEVER promote to ANALYSIS-*.md without user confirmation.
Confirm relevance before investing in a full write-up; a well-reasoned out-of-scope ruling is as valuable as a full summary.
Quote README and docs as evidence; never infer capabilities the author does not describe.
Do not use this skill for a tool already triaged, a tool clearly out of scope, or a full deep dive (triage first, then promote).
